title: Gradual weight shard out-of-sync rollback retrospective
summary: Short narrative of incident — during a staggered gradual rollout of model v2.1.0 we observed a divergence in weight shards across nodes leading to increasing inference error rates and intermittent 5xx errors for a subset of requests. The issue was traced to an out-of-sync shard upload step in the deployer which applied a replacement weight file to half the replicas while a background reshard process moved shards on the same hosts. This produced a transient state where some replicas served mixed-weight parameters. Emergency rollback to v2.0.7 and a resync of signed weight artifacts restored normal service.
impact:
- Duration: ~55 minutes of elevated errors (2025-02-14T13:02 - 2025-02-14T13:57 UTC)
- Affected customers: approximately 3% of requests routed to us during the window saw higher semantic drift (embedding cosine drop ~0.12) and ~0.8% 5xx rate increase on shard-heavy inference paths
- Surface areas: hosting API text-generation latency tail spikes and a small number of failed batch jobs on Dedicated pools
detection:
- Alerts: model-quality regression detector (eval-runner) alerted at 2025-02-14T13:04 UTC
- SRE noticed increased 5xx counts on model-serving LB at 13:07 UTC
- Customer report: one enterprise customer (CustAcme) opened a support ticket at 13:16 UTC noting increased failure rates
timeline: 2025-02-14T12:45 UTC: Rollout v2.1.0 started using staged rolling updater: workers replaced in 10% increments with post-deploy preflight checks disabled (optimization flag true).
2025-02-14T12:59 UTC: First 10% batch deployed; no immediate alerts.
2025-02-14T13:02 UTC: Eval-runner data pipeline detected semantic regression in the canary prompt set (drop in embedding cohesion). Automated alert sent to #sre-incident-2789.
2025-02-14T13:04 UTC: On-call SRE (Priya) triaged alerts; noted correlation with hosts running mixed shard indices.
2025-02-14T13:10 UTC: Higher 5xx rate observed on subset of replicas; partial traffic steering initiated to reduce load on suspected hosts (manual LB rule).

2025-02-14T13:18 UTC: Investigation discovered that deployer uploaded weight file parts to /weights/tmp then moved them into place; a background resharding job used the same temp prefix and occasionally renamed shards in flight, creating partial apply windows.
2025-02-14T13:25 UTC: Attempted in-place re-sync of weight artifacts on affected hosts (rsync + checksum); discovered inconsistent checksums across replicas for shard files.
2025-02-14T13:33 UTC: Decided to rollback to v2.0.7 for the remaining rollout cohorts; rollback began.
2025-02-14T13:42 UTC: Rollback completed for all cohorts; monitoring showed error rates returning to baseline by 13:57 UTC.
2025-02-14T14:05 UTC: Post-incident meeting scheduled; began drafting this retrospective.
root_cause: Operational race between deployer artifact move semantics and an asynchronous reshard background job. The deployer used a naive atomic-rename strategy that assumed exclusive ownership of the temp prefix. The resharder also used the same temp prefix for partial writes and occasionally moved partially-complete shard files onto live paths. Lack of a signed checksum preflight and disabled preflight checks during rollout amplified impact.
mitigation_and_remediation: Immediate: paused rollout, reverted traffic via LB rules, rolled remaining cohorts back to v2.0.7, run full rsync+checksum re-deploy of v2.1.0 artifacts in a staging environment to validate fix before re-attempting.

Short-term (next 72h): enforce preflight checksum compare on deployer (re-enable preflight checks by default), update deployer to use unique temp prefixes per process and per shard, add guard that blocks resharder from operating on temp prefixes.

Long-term: extend artifact signing to include per-shard signatures and enforce signature verification in the runtime loader; change rolling updater to validate checksums before marking a replica healthy.
actions_taken: Alert triage and on-call coordination (13:04 - Priya Nair)
Traffic steering away from suspects (13:10 - Liam O'Connor)
Checksum audit and partial rsync attempts (13:25 - Zara Chen)
Decision to rollback and execution of rollback (13:33 - whole SRE + deployer team)
postmortem_notes:
- Gap: deployer and resharder assumed disjoint temp paths; this was not enforced in code.
- Observability: checksums were computed in artifact storage but not surfaced in runtime or rollout dashboards; add checks to dashboards.
- Customer communication: a post-incident notice was sent to impacted customers at 2025-02-15 09:12 PST (CS ticket CS-5412).
follow_up_actions: INF-2792: Add per-shard signed artifact format + loader verification (owner: engineering-applied-ml, due: 2025-03-07)
INF-2793: Deployer: unique temp prefix + atomic swap refactor (owner: platform-engineering, due: 2025-02-21)
INF-2794: Resharder: avoid operating on temp prefixes + add locking (owner: serving-runtime, due: 2025-02-28)
INF-2795: Dashboard: expose per-shard checksum mismatch metric and rollout preflight pass rate (owner: observability, due: 2025-03-01)
INF-2796: Post-release blackout period policy update — disable preflight skip by default (owner: product, due: 2025-02-17)
runbook_changes: Add step: preflight checksum verification BEFORE cutover for every shard
Add step: if any checksum mismatch detected, automatically pause rollout and route traffic to last-known-good model
Add step: define temp-prefix ownership contract; resharder must use distinct temp locations or acquire a lock
notes_to_oncall: Quick triage checklist added to runbook: 1) check artifact store checksums 2) check resharder logs for concurrent writes 3) steer traffic 4) re-sync or rollback
Remind: do not attempt ad-hoc partial in-place fixes without team coordination — rsync attempts can amplify divergence if not coordinated
Escalation: if rollback fails or >5% of customer requests affected, page EngLead and Exec oncall
open_questions: Why was preflight disabled for this rollout? (owner: product-deploy-priority) — we saw a CLI flag set to true; need to trace decision
Are there other background jobs that use the same temp prefix pattern? (owner: platform-engineering)
Can we implement a runtime-only guard that refuses to load shards without valid per-shard signatures?
